greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Ιακωβ Ἀναστὰς ἀνάβηθι εἰς τὸν τόπον Βαιθηλ καὶ οἴκει ἐκεῖ καὶ ποίησον ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον τῷ θεῷ τῷ ὀφθέντι σοι ἐν τῷ ἀποδιδράσκειν σε ἀπὸ προσώπου Ησαυ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
hint: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel, dwell there, and make an altar to the God who appeared to him fleeing Esau.

notes.text: ἀποδιδράσκω, *to run away*, of a slave or a fugitive; ἐν τῷ with the infinitive, the one place the article before an infinitive is printed here.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")
(Βαιθηλ, from Hebrew Bêt-ʾĒl, "house of God")
(Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιακωβ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ Ἄρατε τοὺς θεοὺς τοὺς ἀλλοτρίους τοὺς μεθʼ ὑμῶν ἐκ μέσου ὑμῶν καὶ καθαρίσασθε καὶ ἀλλάξατε τὰς στολὰς ὑμῶν,
hint: Jacob tells his household to put away their foreign gods, purify themselves, and change their clothes.

notes.text: ἀλλότριος, *belonging to another*: the gods are another's, not that they are false.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits τοὺς μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἀναστάντες ἀναβῶμεν εἰς Βαιθηλ καὶ ποιήσωμεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον τῷ θεῷ τῷ ἐπακούσαντί μοι ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως, ὃς ἦν μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ διέσωσέν με ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ᾗ ἐπορεύθην.
hint: Jacob calls them up to Bethel, to make an altar to the God who heard him in distress and kept him on the road.

notes.text: Middle Liddell has θλίβω but not the noun; LSJ gives θλῖψις *pressure*, *crushing*, *oppression, affliction*, and cites this very verse for the third.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐπορευόμην, the imperfect.

greek: καὶ ἔδωκαν τῷ Ιακωβ τοὺς θεοὺς τοὺς ἀλλοτρίους, οἳ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ ἐνώτια τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν αὐτῶν, καὶ κατέκρυψεν αὐτὰ Ιακωβ ὑπὸ τὴν τερέμινθον τὴν ἐν Σικιμοις καὶ ἀπώλεσεν αὐτὰ ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
hint: Jacob hides the foreign gods and earrings under the terebinth at Shechem, and destroys them to this day.

notes.text: ἐνώτιον, *an earring*, one sense; the word is the neuter of ἐν + οὖς, in the ear.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus writes β for μ, τερέβινθον; Rahlfs keeps μ, as at 14:6 and 43:11.

names.gloss: (Σικιμα, from Hebrew Šĕkem, "shoulder")

greek: καὶ ἐξῆρεν Ισραηλ ἐκ Σικιμων, καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος θεοῦ ἐπὶ τὰς πόλεις τὰς κύκλῳ αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ κατεδίωξαν ὀπίσω τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: Israel sets out from Shechem; a fear of God lies on the cities round about, and none pursue.

notes.text: ἐξαίρω, *to lift up, lift off the earth*, here with no object: Israel lifted up from Shechem. LSJ gives a seemingly intransitive *start*, of an army, citing Numbers 2:9; Middle Liddell, the reading's lexicon, does not.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: ἦλθεν δὲ Ιακωβ εἰς Λουζα, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν γῇ Χανααν, ἥ ἐστιν Βαιθηλ, αὐτὸς καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαός, ὃς ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Jacob and all his people come to Luz, which is Bethel, in the land of Canaan.

notes.text: The Greek keeps the old name beside the new, as the Hebrew does: Luz is Bethel.

reading: [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near|ἔρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Λουζα]], which is [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[to earth|to earth, to land, to ground|γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]], which is [[name:Βαιθηλ]], he and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of him.

names.gloss: (Λουζα, from Hebrew Lûz, usually connected with lûz, "almond tree")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου Βαιθηλ· ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἐπεφάνη αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῷ ἀποδιδράσκειν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ προσώπου Ησαυ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Jacob builds an altar and names the place Bethel, where God appeared to him fleeing Esau.

notes.text: ἐπιφαίνω, *to shew forth*, in the passive *to come suddenly into view*: it is the word of a sudden showing, not of a vision sought.

greek: ἀπέθανεν δὲ Δεββωρα ἡ τροφὸς Ρεβεκκας κατώτερον Βαιθηλ ὑπὸ τὴν βάλανον, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Ιακωβ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Βάλανος πένθους.
hint: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies below Bethel under the oak, which Jacob names Oak of Mourning.

notes.text: βάλανος, *an acorn*, and so the oak that bears it; the name Jacob gives it is the common noun with Rahlfs's capital.
The comparative of κάτω as an adverb with the genitive: below Bethel.

reading: [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Δεββωρα]] [[the feeder|the feeder, the rearer, the nurse|τροφός]] of [[name:Ρεβεκκας]] [[lower|lower, more southerly, later and younger|κατώτερος]] of [[name:Βαιθηλ]] [[towards and under|towards and under, under and into, under and before, under, in subjection, towards, about, about the time, to a certain degree and in some measure|ὑπό + accusative]] [[the acorn|the acorn, the similar fruit and date, the iron peg and bolt-pin|βάλανος]], and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of her [[name:Βάλανος]] [[of grief|of grief, of sadness, of sorrow, of mourning for, of a public mourning, of a misfortune|πένθος]].

(Ρεβεκκα, from Hebrew Ribqâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Βάλανος πένθους, "acorn of mourning", the Greek of Hebrew ʾAllôn-bākût, the oak of weeping)

greek: Ὤφθη δὲ ὁ θεὸς Ιακωβ ἔτι ἐν Λουζα, ὅτε παρεγένετο ἐκ Μεσοποταμίας τῆς Συρίας, καὶ ηὐλόγησεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός.
hint: God appears to Jacob again at Luz, on his return from Mesopotamia of Syria, and blesses him.

notes.text: The aorist passive of ὁράω, *was seen*: the Greek says God was seen, where English says he appeared.

(Συρία, the Greek name of the land; the Hebrew here is Paddan-ʾĂrām)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεός Τὸ ὄνομά σου Ιακωβ· οὐ κληθήσεται ἔτι Ιακωβ, ἀλλʼ Ισραηλ ἔσται τὸ ὄνομά σου.
hint: God confirms the new name: no longer Jacob, but Israel.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits the first Ιακωβ.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of you [[name:Ιακωβ]]; not [[will be called|will be called, will be summoned, will be invited|καλέω]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly|ἀλλά]] [[name:Ισραηλ]] will be [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of you.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός Ἐγὼ ὁ θεός σου· αὐξάνου καὶ πληθύνου· ἔθνη καὶ συναγωγαὶ ἐθνῶν ἔσονται ἐκ σοῦ, καὶ βασιλεῖς ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος σου ἐξελεύσονται.
hint: God bids Jacob grow and multiply; nations, gatherings of nations and kings will come from him.

notes.text: ὀσφῦς, *the loin*; Middle Liddell notes that the fruit of the loins is a son.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts καί before ἔθνη.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ τὴν γῆν, ἣν δέδωκα Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ, σοὶ δέδωκα αὐτήν· σοὶ ἔσται, καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σὲ δώσω τὴν γῆν ταύτην.
hint: God gives Jacob and his seed after him the land given to Abraham and Isaac.

notes.text: The perfect of δίδωμι twice over: the giving stands done, a settled state, not an act now performed.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits σοὶ ἔσται.

reading: and [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], which [[I have given|I have given and it stands given, I have granted and it stands granted, I have provided and it stands provided, I have given over and delivered up and it stands so|δίδωμι]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] and to [[name:Ισαακ]], to you [[I have given|I have given and it stands given, I have granted and it stands granted, I have provided and it stands provided, I have given over and delivered up and it stands so|δίδωμι]] her; to you will be, and [[to the that which is sown|to the that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]].

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")
(Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")

greek: ἀνέβη δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ τόπου, οὗ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
hint: God goes up from Jacob, from the place where he spoke with him.

notes.text: ἀναβαίνω, *to go up*: the same verb as the command of 35:1, now of God himself.

reading: [[went up|went up, mounted, ascended, went up to, rose, came up, came to and arrived at, went up country, went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of him [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity|τόπος]], where [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of him.

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Ιακωβ στήλην ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, ᾧ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ, στήλην λιθίνην, καὶ ἔσπεισεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν σπονδὴν καὶ ἐπέχεεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν ἔλαιον.
hint: Jacob sets up a stone pillar where God spoke with him, and pours a drink offering and oil on it.

notes.text: στήλη, *a block of stone*, first the thing itself and then what it marks.
σπένδω, *to pour a drink-offering*; the middle of the same verb is *to make a treaty*, since treaties were sealed by pouring.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Ιακωβ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου, ἐν ᾧ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ ὁ θεός, Βαιθηλ.
hint: Jacob names the place where God spoke with him Bethel.

notes.text: The name is given twice in the chapter, at 35:7 and here; the Greek repeats what the Hebrew repeats.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity|τόπος]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to which [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of him [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]], [[name:Βαιθηλ]].

greek: Ἀπάρας δὲ Ιακωβ ἐκ Βαιθηλ ἔπηξεν τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπέκεινα τοῦ πύργου Γαδερ. ἐγένετο δὲ ἡνίκα ἤγγισεν χαβραθα εἰς γῆν ἐλθεῖν Εφραθα, ἔτεκεν Ραχηλ καὶ ἐδυστόκησεν ἐν τῷ τοκετῷ.
hint: Leaving Bethel, Jacob camps beyond the tower of Gader; nearing Ephrath, Rachel gives birth in hard labour.

notes.text: The Hebrew kibrat, a stretch of ground of unknown length, carried into Greek untranslated; the printed page has it in lower case, where the digital module capitalises it, and the transcription follows the page.
δυστοκέω, one sense, *to be in sore travail*, said of women.

reading: [[having lifted off|having lifted off, having carried off, having taken away, having removed from, having led away, having sailed and marched away and departed, having departed from, having set out on|ἀπαίρω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of [[name:Βαιθηλ]] [[made fast|made fast, fixed in the earth and planted, fastened together and constructed and built, made solid and stiff and hard, froze, became solid and stiff, became congealed and froze|πήγνυμι]] [[the covered place|the covered place, the tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple|σκηνή]] of him [[on yonder side|on yonder side, beyond, the part beyond and the far side|ἐπέκεινα]] [[of the tower|of the tower, of the city walls with towers, of the movable tower for storming, of the tower of defence, of the highest part of any building, of the troops drawn up in close order and the column|πύργος]] of [[name:Γαδερ]]. [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[brought near|brought near, brought up to, approached, was imminent, approximated to, was next of kin, was on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] [[name:χαβραθα]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[earth|earth, land, ground|γῆ]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near|ἔρχομαι]] of [[name:Εφραθα]], [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, begot, produced and yielded|τίκτω]] [[name:Ραχηλ]] and was in sore travail [[in the birth|within, inside of, and by means of the birth, the delivery|ἐν; τοκετός]].

names.gloss: (Γαδερ, from Hebrew ʿĒder, "flock")
(χαβραθα, the Hebrew kibrat left untranslated, a stretch of ground of unknown length)
(Εφραθα, from Hebrew ʾEprātâ, usually connected with pārâ, "to be fruitful")
(Ραχηλ, from Hebrew Rāḥēl, "ewe")

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ σκληρῶς αὐτὴν τίκτειν εἶπεν αὐτῇ ἡ μαῖα Θάρσει, καὶ γὰρ οὗτός σοί ἐστιν υἱός.
hint: The midwife bids Rachel, in her hard labour, take courage: this one too is a son.

notes.text: μαῖα, *good mother, dame* first, and *a midwife* last: the word is a form of address before it is a trade.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits σοί.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[hard|hard, hard and harsh and crashing, hard and stiff and unyielding, stiff and sturdy, hard and austere and severe|σκληρῶς]] her [[the bringing into the world|the bringing into the world, the bringing forth, the bearing, the begetting, the producing and yielding|τίκτω]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to her [[the good mother|the good mother, the dame, the fostermother and nurse, the true mother, the midwife|μαῖα]] [[be of good courage|be of good courage, take courage, be over-bold and audacious, have confidence in, venture|θαρσέω]], and [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] to you is son.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἀφιέναι αὐτὴν τὴν ψυχήν — ἀπέθνῃσκεν γάρ — ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Υἱὸς ὀδύνης μου· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸν Βενιαμιν.
hint: As her soul leaves her, Rachel names the boy 'Son of my pain'; his father calls him Benjamin.

notes.text: Rahlfs capitalises Υἱὸς: the phrase is the name, the Greek of Hebrew Ben-ʾÔnî.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds αὐτοῦ, *his*, marked in the Hexaplaric text with an asterisk.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[the sending forth|the sending forth, the discharging, the letting go and loose and setting free, the letting go as an aphetos (ἄφετος) and consecrating, the letting alone and leaving, the giving up and handing over, the permitting and allowing|ἀφίημι]] her [[the breath|the breath, the life, the spirit, life and death, the ghost, the departed soul|ψυχή]] — [[was dying off|was dying off, was dying, was being put to death, was being slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] — [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Υἱὸς]] [[of pain of body|of pain of body, of pain of mind, of grief and distress|ὀδύνη]] of me; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] him [[name:Βενιαμιν]].

names.gloss: (Υἱὸς ὀδύνης μου, "son of my pain", the Greek of Hebrew Ben-ʾÔnî)
(Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: ἀπέθανεν δὲ Ραχηλ καὶ ἐτάφη ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ Εφραθα (αὕτη ἐστὶν Βηθλεεμ).
hint: Rachel dies and is buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

notes.text: θάπτω is first *to pay the last dues to a corpse, to honour with funeral rites*, then *to bury*: the word covers the rite as well as the act.

reading: [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ραχηλ]] and [[had the last dues paid|had the last dues paid to a corpse, was honoured with funeral rites, was buried and interred|θάπτω]] [[in the way|within, inside of, and by means of the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method|ἐν; ὁδός]] of [[name:Εφραθα]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] is [[name:Βηθλεεμ]]).

names.gloss: (Βηθλεεμ, from Hebrew Bêt-Leḥem, "house of bread")

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Ιακωβ στήλην ἐπὶ τοῦ μνημείου αὐτῆς· αὕτη ἐστὶν στήλη μνημείου Ραχηλ ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
hint: Jacob sets a pillar on Rachel's tomb, which stands there to this day.

notes.text: μνημεῖον, *a memorial*, as at 23:6: the thing that keeps the memory, before it is a grave.

reading: and [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed|ἵστημι]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[block of stone|block of stone, prop and buttress to a wall, slab, gravestone, record and contract and agreement, turning-post|στήλη]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the memorial|of the memorial, of the remembrance, of the record, of the monument|μνημεῖον]] of her; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] is [[block of stone|block of stone, prop and buttress to a wall, slab, gravestone, record and contract and agreement, turning-post|στήλη]] [[of memorial|of memorial, of remembrance, of record, of monument|μνημεῖον]] of [[name:Ραχηλ]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as|ἕως]] of the to-day [[of day|of day, of day-break, of time|ἡμέρα]].

greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡνίκα κατῴκησεν Ισραηλ ἐν τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ, ἐπορεύθη Ρουβην καὶ ἐκοιμήθη μετὰ Βαλλας τῆς παλλακῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἤκουσεν Ισραηλ, καὶ πονηρὸν ἐφάνη ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ. Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα.
hint: Reuben sleeps with his father's concubine Bilhah, and Israel hears and takes it ill. Jacob's sons are twelve.

notes.text: The neuter as a noun with φαίνω: a toilsome thing appeared, where the Hebrew says simply that Israel heard.

notes.lemma: Ἦσαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα
notes.text: The sentence stands in the same verse as Reuben's act, with nothing between them: the twelve are counted where the offence is told.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[dwelt in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|dwelt in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate|κατοικέω]] [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the earth, the land, the ground|ἐν; γῆ]] [[to that|to that, to the one there, to the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]], [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed|πορεύομαι]] [[name:Ρουβην]] and [[was lulled|was lulled, was hushed to sleep and put to sleep, was lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, fell asleep, went abed and lay abed, slept, fell asleep and died, kept watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of [[name:Βαλλας]] [[of the concubine|of the concubine, of the mistress|παλλακή]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him; and [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, knew by hearsay, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[name:Ισραηλ]], and [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked|πονηρός]] [[was brought to light|was brought to light and made to appear, was shown forth and made known and revealed and disclosed and shown, was made clear and explained and expounded, was informed against and indicted and impeached, was proclaimed, came to light and was seen and appeared, shone brightly, came into being, appeared to be, was manifest|φαίνω]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of him. were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, the sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] twelve.

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Βαλλα, from Hebrew Bilhâ, usually connected with bāhal, "to be troubled")

greek: υἱοὶ Λειας· πρωτότοκος Ιακωβ Ρουβην, Συμεων, Λευι, Ιουδας, Ισσαχαρ, Ζαβουλων.
hint: Leah's six sons, from Reuben the firstborn to Zebulun.

notes.text: πρωτότοκος, *firstborn*, the word that carries the whole of Genesis's quarrel over birthright.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Λευεις.

reading: sons of [[name:Λειας]]; [[firstborn|firstborn, first-fruits|πρωτότοκος]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[name:Ρουβην]], [[name:Συμεων]], [[name:Λευι]], [[name:Ιουδας]], [[name:Ισσαχαρ]], [[name:Ζαβουλων]].

names.gloss: (Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")
(Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")
(Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")
(Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ραχηλ· Ιωσηφ καὶ Βενιαμιν.
hint: Rachel's two sons, Joseph and Benjamin.

notes.text: The list runs without a verb throughout 35:23-26: the Greek keeps the Hebrew's bare naming.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and [[name:Βενιαμιν]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Βαλλας παιδίσκης Ραχηλ· Δαν καὶ Νεφθαλι.
hint: Bilhah's two sons, Dan and Naphtali.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Νεφθαλειμ.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Βαλλας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl, of a maiden, of a young slave, of a courtesan|παιδίσκη]] of [[name:Ραχηλ]]; [[name:Δαν]] and [[name:Νεφθαλι]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")
(Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ζελφας παιδίσκης Λειας· Γαδ καὶ Ασηρ. οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ιακωβ, οἳ ἐγένοντο αὐτῷ ἐν Μεσοποταμίᾳ τῆς Συρίας.
hint: Zilpah's two sons, Gad and Asher; these are Jacob's sons, born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.

notes.text: [[flag]] All twelve are said to have been born in Mesopotamia, though Benjamin was born at Ephrath in 35:16-18; the Hebrew says the same.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Ζελφας]] [[of a young girl|of a young girl, of a maiden, of a young slave, of a courtesan|παιδίσκη]] of [[name:Λειας]]; [[name:Γαδ]] and [[name:Ασηρ]]. [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]], which [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Μεσοποταμίᾳ]] of the [[name:Συρίας]].

names.gloss: (Ζελφα, from Hebrew Zilpâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")
(Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Ἦλθεν δὲ Ιακωβ πρὸς Ισαακ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ εἰς Μαμβρη εἰς πόλιν τοῦ πεδίου (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν γῇ Χανααν, οὗ παρῴκησεν Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ.
hint: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.

notes.text: παροικέω, *to dwell beside*, of a resident alien: neither man ever owned the land he lived in.

reading: [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near|ἔρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Μαμβρη]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[city|city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state|πόλις]] [[of the plain|of the plain, of the flat, of the plain flat open country|πεδίον]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[to earth|to earth, to land, to ground|γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]], where [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned|παροικέω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Ισαακ]].

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥābar, "to join")

greek: ἐγένοντο δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι Ισαακ, ἃς ἔζησεν, ἔτη ἑκατὸν ὀγδοήκοντα·
hint: Isaac lives a hundred and eighty years.

notes.text: ζάω, *to live*, with the days as its object: the Greek counts the days he lived, not the years he was.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times|ἡμέρα]] of [[name:Ισαακ]], which [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong|ζάω]], years hundred eighty;

greek: καὶ ἐκλιπὼν ἀπέθανεν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν, καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν Ησαυ καὶ Ιακωβ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Isaac dies at a great age and is added to his kin; his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

notes.text: ἐκλείπω, *to leave out*, and so *to fail, die away*: the Greek says he left off before it says he died.
προστίθημι in the passive, *was put to*: the dead man is added to his kin, as at 25:8 and 25:17.

reading: and [[having left out|having left out, having omitted and passed over, having forsaken and deserted and abandoned, having suffered an eclipse, having died, having left off and ceased and stopped, having failed and been wanting|ἐκλείπω]] [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] and [[was put to|was put to, was handed over and delivered, was given and bestowed, was imposed further, was attributed, was added|προστίθημι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the race|the race, the stock and family, the offspring and posterity, the clan and house, the tribe and caste, the breed, the age and generation, the sex and gender, the class and sort and kind, the genus|γένος]] of him [[elder|elder, older, higher and more important, greater than, elders of the Jewish Council, elders of the Church and presbyters|πρεσβύτερος]] and [[full|full, filled, complete, satisfied, whole and entire|πλήρης]] [[of days|of days, of day-breaks, of times|ἡμέρα]], and [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse, honoured with funeral rites, buried, interred|θάπτω]] him [[name:Ησαυ]] and [[name:Ιακωβ]] the sons of him.
